summary: Nathan Sivin worked in sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at the Defense Language Institute, MIT, Harvard, and Kyoto University. He taught at MIT from 1966 to 1977, became Professor Emeritus at the University of Pennsylvania (1977-2006), and was Honorary Professor at CAS (~1999-2022).

Nathan W. Hill works in linguistics, Tibetology, and sinology. He studied at Harvard (~2001-2009) under Leonard van der Kuijp and Jay Jasanoff. He served as Principal Investigator at SOAS (~2008-2019) and Trinity College Dublin (~2019), also holding posts there and visiting professorships at Berkeley and Oxford.

Nathaniel Brassey Halhed was an Indologist and linguist. He was educated at Harrow School and studied at Christ Church in 1768. From approximately 1771 to 1785, he served as an official for the East India Company.

Nathaniel DeWitt Garson is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia, where he was supervised by Jeffrey Hopkins, and also studied under the traditional teacher Khenpo Namdrol.
Nathaniel Wallich studied at the University of Copenhagen. He served as Superintendent at the Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden from approximately 1817 to 1846.

Nathmal Tatia was an Indologist and scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He earned a Doctor of Literature from the University of Calcutta, studying under Satkari Mookerjee and Sukhlal Sanghvi, and served as Director of the Jain Vishva Bharati Institute (attested 1982-1990).
Navina Lamminger is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Munich under the doctoral supervision of Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

Nawang Tsering Shakspo works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his doctoral studies under Lal Mani Joshi and served as a Lecturer at the Central Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 1985).
Nazir Ahmad Dehlvi was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Delhi under Mamluk Ali Nanautawi from approximately 1845 to 1853. He later taught Ghulam Yazdani.
Neal Donner is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at the University of British Columbia under Leon Hurvitz (attested 1976).
Neelima Mundayar is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. She is a PhD student at the University of Edinburgh under the doctoral supervision of Wilfried Swenden (attested 2026).

Nenghai Shi worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Peking University (~1914-1915) and under Kecheng Zhang, Foyuan, Guanyi, and Khangsar Dorje Chang. He founded the Shaocheng Society of Buddhist Studies in 1917 and served as vice-president of the Buddhist Association of China (1953-1966).
Newton Mohun Dutt worked in Indology. He held the post of Curator of Libraries for Baroda State and at the Central Library of Vadodara from approximately 1914 to 1934.
Ng-Fung Yuen is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned a PhD from the University of the West under the doctoral supervision of Kottegoda S. Warnasuriya (attested 2009).
Ngakchang Gönpo Tsé Ten studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche.
Ngan-che Chan is a scholar of Buddhist studies. Chan earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the doctoral supervision of Jing Yin and also studied under K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2007).
Ngawang Jorden is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held a post at Sakya College and served as director of the International Buddhist Academy.
Ngawang Lek Shé Gyatso studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, and Trulshik Rinpoche.

Ngawang Nyima was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, the 14th Dalai Lama, and Trijang Rinpoche. He taught Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima, Thubten Jigme Norbu, and Dagpo Rinpoche.

Ngorpa Pönlob Lo Ter Wangpo studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Shechen Gyaltsab, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He taught Shenphen Nangwa and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.
